en: Using an inclined plane like a ramp reduces the force needed to lift heavy boxes, preventing back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the ground, which helps prevent dangerous slipping on wet bathroom floors.
Storing heavy objects on lower shelves prevents them from falling and causing head injuries due to Earth's gravity.
Swallowing small neodymium magnets is extremely dangerous because they can attract each other and pinch intestinal walls.
Because water conducts electricity well, you must never touch plugged-in appliances with wet hands to avoid severe shocks.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without certified eclipse glasses can cause permanent, irreversible damage to your retina.
Listening to headphones at maximum volume for over an hour can permanently damage the delicate hair cells inside your ears.
Dark-colored clothing absorbs more heat radiation from the sun, making you feel uncomfortably hot during outdoor recess.
Your body converts the chemical energy stored in bananas into the kinetic energy you need to run and play.
A wheelbarrow acts as a second-class lever, allowing you to move heavy garden soil with much less physical effort.
Touching a metal doorknob after walking on a carpet safely discharges built-up static electricity as a tiny shock.
Metal spoon handles get hot quickly because metals are excellent conductors of thermal energy from your hot soup.
